violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. A food employee at the grill handled the following items with the same pair of gloves: raw beef patty, salt shaker, raw chicken, salt shaker.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. The EHS discussed the correct way tot handle these foods during the inspection. The PIC passed the information on to the employee.

violations.title: Chemical Sanitizing, Contact Time Met
violations.observation: The outside bar warewashing machine on the left was not working properly. The chlorine sanitizer concentration was 0 ppm after running it a few times.
violations.corrective_action: Chemical sanitization (manual or mechanical operations) including the application of sanitizing chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods using a solution by providing: 1) an exposure time of at least 10 seconds for a chlorine solution, 2) an exposure time of at least 7 seconds for a chlorine solution of 50mg/L that has a pH of 10 or less and a water temperature of 100F or a pH of 8 or less and a water temperature of 75F, 3) an exposure time of at least 30 seconds for other chemical sanitizing solutions, or 4) an exposure time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and pH that when evaluated for efficacy yields sanitization. The PIC called the service company during the inspection to have the unit serviced and placed a sign on it telling employees not to use it until it’s fixed. CDI.

violations.title: Food Contact Surfaces Clean to Sight & Touch
violations.observation: The following equipment/utensils were observed soiled to sight and touch: the slicer was “clean” but was visibly soiled with food debris.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to the sight and touch. A surface that is soiled cannot be effectively sanitized. The PIC had the slicer cleaned and sanitized during the inspection. CDI.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: whole cooked chicken in the hot holding cabinet was not hot enough at 121º.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. The PIC had the chicken reheated in the oven during the inspection. CDI.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: chili and queso made yesterday were not cold enough in the walk-in at 46º and 54ºF. Short ribs in the walk-in were not being held cold enough in the walk-in at 49º. Chicken wings cooked yesterday were 49ºF in the walk-in. Foods in the 2-drawer unit under the griddle were no being held cold enough. Cooked sliced chicken was 48º. Mahi mahi was 47º.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. All the foods listed above were discarded. Foods in the griddle drawer unit were previously in the walk-in, which was not working properly, which is why they were discarded.

violations.title: Food Thermometer, Repair and Calibration
violations.observation: The thermometer on the hot holding cabinet under the hood was not working.
violations.corrective_action: Food thermometers shall be calibrated in accordance with manufacturer's specifications as necessary to ensure their accuracy. It is suggested that food thermometers be calibrated at least once a week in a cup completely filled with ice and cold water to a temperature of 32F or calibrated in a pot of boiling water at 212F. Repair or replace the thermometer, or install a second one in the unit. The manager installed a second thermometer during the inspection.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Handled scoops were being used to dispense ice at the bar and ingredients (flour, bread crumbs, salt) from large containers in the kitchen. The scoop handles were being stored in the foods, which is not permitted. Also, in-use utensils were being stored in 135º hot water, but the water was visibly soiled and needed to be changed.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. This was corrected during the inspection. CDI.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: the ambient temperature of the walk-in was 45º and foods in it were not being held cold enough at 41º and above. One of the bar dishmachines was not working properly.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. Have both units serviced as soon as possible and notify your EHS when they have been serviced and are working properly.

violations.title: Backflow Prevention, Air Gap Provided
violations.observation: Observed a hose attached to a faucet fixture. The hose extended below the flood rim level of the sink basin.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be installed to preclude backflow of a solid, liquid, or gas contaminant into the water supply system at each point of use at the food establishment, including on a hose bib if a hose is attached or on a hose bib if a hose is not attached and backflow prevention is required by Law by providing an air gap as specified under 5-202.13. The PIC corrected this during the inspection.

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching coughing into her hand.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. The EHS brought this to the attention of the CFM, who had the employee was her hands.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Designated Use
violations.observation: Observed the handsink at the front of the kitchen being used to rinse a knife off and to dump onions in.
violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. The EHS discussed us with the CFM. CDI.

violations.title: Chemical Sanitization, Chlorine Requirements
violations.observation: When tested, the low temperature, chemical sanitizing warewashing machine was observed with a sanitizing rinse concentration of less than 50 ppm chlorine solution. The solution was 0 parts per million chlorine. The left side glass washing machine at the bar was not sanitizing . The chlorine solution was 0 ppm.
violations.corrective_action: Immediately discontinue use of the dishmachine. Until the machine is adequately repaired, set up the three-compartment sink to manually wash, rinse and sanitize food-contact surfaces using a sanitizing solution at the proper concentration of at least 50 to 200 ppm total chlorine. The CFM was able to prime the dishwasher and resolve this issue during the inspection. The concentration of the final rinse was 50 ppm before the end of the inspection. The manager decided to stop using the machine on the left side and run all glasses through the machine on the right side, which is working properly. Have the machine on the left side serviced as soon as possible.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: the barbecue chicken on the hot holding unit was 125°F
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. The CFM corrected this by reheating the barbecue chicken to 165°F.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: the following foods were not being held cold enough in the far left prep top unit: ranch dressing was 47°, blue cheese crumbles were 53°, cut tomatoes were 46°. The following foods were not being held cold enough in the left middle prep top refrigerator: sliced tomatoes were 51°F, beef patties were 45°F, raw salmon was 50°F, raw chicken was 52°F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. The sliced tomatoes were from yesterday and were discarded. All other foods were placed in the walk-in to cool down. CDI.

violations.title: Food Thermometers Accuracy, Degrees C & F
violations.observation: There were several inaccurate thermometers in refrigeration units. The digital thermometers on the first two prep refrigerators were not working properly and not readable. The two thermometers in the walker refrigerator were inaccurate.
violations.corrective_action: Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Celsius or dually scaled in Celsius and Fahrenheit shall be accurate to +/- 1 degree C in the intended range of use. Repair the thermometers if possible, replaced them, or install additional thermometers that are accurate.

violations.title: Hair Restraints
violations.observation: Employees observed working in the food service area without proper hair restraints. There was one food handler who was not wearing a hair restraint while working with foods.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wear hair restraints such as hats, visors, hair nets or beard nets to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service items. This section does not apply to food employees such as counter staff who ONLY serve beverages and wrapped or packaged foods, hostesses, and wait staff. Correct by the follow-up. OPEN ROAD (Inspection Date: 11/24/2025) Page 3 of 4

violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.' FACILITY UNABLE TO PROVIDE EMPLOYEE HEALTH POLICIES AT TIME OF INSPECTION.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. EMPLOYEE HEALTH POLICIES SHOULD BE KEPT ONSITE FOR EHS TO REVIEW DURING INSPECTIONS. ENSURE POLICIES ARE AVAILABLE FOR EHS TO REVIEW DURING FOLLOW-UP INSPECTION.

EHS ALSO STRESSED NOT DOUBLE OR TRIPLE PANNING FOODS. FOODS WERE REHEATED TO 165F OR ABOVE. ENSURE CORRECT HOT HOLDING TEMPERATURES BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: 1) LIME CREMA IN A COLD WELL: 60F, 2) PORTIONED CUPS OF HOMEMADE BLEU CHEESE DRESSING: 58F, 3) RAW MEATBALLS INSIDE A 2DRAWER UNIT AT THE COOK LINE: 45F-50F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. EHS DISCUSSED COLD FOOD TEMPERATURES. FOODS SHALL BE HELD AT 41F OR BELOW AT ALL TIMES UNLESS COOLING. IF COOLING THE FOODS SHALL BE STORED IN A WALK-IN UNIT OR FREEZER TO ACHIEVE RAPID CHILLING TO 41F BEFORE BEING PLACED ON THE COOK LINE. EHS ALSO DISCUSSED NOT OVERSTOCKING THE PANS OF FOODS AND KEEPING THE LIDS CLOSED WHEN NOT BUSY WITH ORDERS. ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP. FOODS WERE EITHER DISCARDED, PLACED ON ICE IF UNDER 4 HOURS FOR TEMPERATURE ABUSE, OR PLACED INSIDE A REFRIGERATOR.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Observed small spray bottles for sanitizer (used for sanitizing dining room tables) not labeled.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. EHS DISCUSSED WITH THE PERSON IN CHARGE LABELING ALL WORKING BOTTLES AND SPRAY BOTTLES OF CHEMICALS BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: 1) EHS OBSERVED LARGE, DEEP PORTIONS OF FOODS IN THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR EITHER COVERED OR IN PANS THAT ARE TOO DEEP, 2) OBSERVED PREP TOP AND REACH-IN UNITS BEING USED FOR COOLING LARGE BATCHES OF PREPARED FOODS LIKE LETTUCE, TOMATOES, ETC.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EHS DISCUSSED PROPER COOLING METHODS TO INCLUDE FOODS BEING PLACED UNCOVERED, ONLY ON SHEET PANS, UTILIZING THE WALK-IN FREEZER OR OTHER FREEZERS, AND STIRRING FOOD TO ENSURE FOODS COOL DOWN RAPIDLY. FOR A HOT FOOD THAT IS FROM 135F TO 70F IN 2 HOURS OR LESS AND FROM 135F TO 41F OR BELOW IN NO MORE THAN A TOTAL OF 6 HOURS. FOR AMBIENT AIR PRODUCTS THAT IS COOLING TO 41F IN 4 HOURS OR LESS. ENSURE CORRECTION AND TRAINING TO STAFF BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

violations.title: Thermometers, Location for Units with TCS foods
violations.observation: There was no temperature measuring device located in the following cold or hot holding equipment: 1) COLD WELL, 2) 1DOOR UNDER COUNTER HOT BOX AT THE COOK LINE.
violations.corrective_action: Cold or hot holding equipment used for the storage of time/temperature control for safety food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one integral or permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display. EHS DISCUSSED WITH THE PERSON IN CHARGE THAT REFRIGERATION UNITS AND HOT HOLDING BOXES SHALL BE EQUIPPED WITH WORKING, ACCURATE, AND VISIBLE THERMOMETERS. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP. OPEN ROAD (Inspection Date: 11/26/2024) Page 4 of 5

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: 1) OBSERVED WORKING CONTAINERS, BULK BINS, BOTTLES, AND/OR SQUEEZE BOTTLES UNLABELED.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. EHS DISCUSSED THAT WORKING CONTAINERS, BULK BINS, BOTTLES, AND SQUEEZE BOTTLES CONTAINING FOOD SHALL BE LABELED AT ALL TIMES. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

violations.title: Hair Restraints
violations.observation: Employees observed working in the food service area without proper hair restraints.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wear hair restraints such as hats, visors, hair nets or beard nets to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service items. This section does not apply to food employees such as counter staff who ONLY serve beverages and wrapped or packaged foods, hostesses, and wait staff. EHS DISCUSSED WITH THE PERSON IN CHARGE THAT ALL COOKS AND FOOD PREPARERS SHALL WEAR HATS OR HAIR NETS. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

violations.title: Jewelry
violations.observation: Employees observed wearing jewelry on their arms and hands while preparing food.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall limit their jewelry to a plain wedding ring while preparing food. Food employees may not wear bracelets, watches, etc. because they can inhibit proper hand washing. EHS DISCUSSED WITH THE PERSON IN CHARGE THAT FOOD PREPARATION STAFF SHALL NOT WEAR ANY JEWELY ON WRISTS SUCH AS WATCHES, BRACELETS, ETC. ENSURE DISCUSSION WITH STAFF AND ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: 1) FOOD SCOOPS LYING IN THE BULK BINS OF FOODS, 2) FOOD SCOOP(S) LYING IN THE ICE BINS AT THE BARS.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EHS DISCUSSED WITH THE PERSON IN CHARGE THAT ALL FOODS SHALL BE DISPENSED USING A FOOD SCOOP EQUIPPED WITH A HANDLE. THE HANDLE WILL SIT UP, OUT OF THE FOOD BETWEEN USES AND BE PROPERLY WASHED, RINSED, AND SANITIZED EVERY 24 HOURS. ENSURE TRAINING AND CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

violations.title: Backflow Prevention, Approved Device Provided
violations.observation: Observed a mop sink with an unapproved splitter on the thread of the mop sink faucet. The system is under constant pressure.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be installed to preclude backflow of a solid, liquid, or gas contaminant into the water supply system at each point of use at the food establishment, including on a hose bib if a hose is attached or on a hose bib if a hose is not attached and backflow prevention is required by Law by installing an approved backflow prevention device as specified under 5-202.14. EHS HAD THE MANAGER ORDER THE PRESSURE BLEEDING DEVICE TO REMOVE PRESSURE BUILDING UP ON THE MOP SINK SYSTEM. ONCE RECEIVED PLEASE INSTALL.

violations.title: Plumbing System, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: Plumbing connections under the 3-VAT SINK piping are leaking.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair. EHS INSTRUCTED MANAGEMENT TO REPAIR THE LEAK BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Toilet facilities properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned

violations.title: Covered Receptacle in Women's Toilet
violations.observation: There is no covered refuse container for the disposal of feminine napkins in the employee’s ladies room stall.
violations.corrective_action: A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. EHS DISCUSSED WITH THE PERSON IN CHARGE PROVIDING A COVERED TRASH CAN IN THE LADIES EMPLOYEE RESTROOM BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: Observed kitchen ceiling panels missing or not securely intact. Observed small gaps/holes in the ceiling panels upstairs in the storage area where electrical wiring is located.
violations.corrective_action: Repair the physical facilities. Poor repair and maintenance compromises the functionality of the physical facilities. EHS DISCUSSED WITH MANAGEMENT REPLACING/REPAIRING MISSING CEILING PANELS AND SEALING UP ANY HOLES/GAPS BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.
